entries.proposition: Claim carried by the abstract-level headline: two de novo CSNK1A1 variants underlie infantile spasms; the exome evidence is two families.
entries.snippet: First, we performed the systematic trios-based WES in two independent ISS families and identified two de novo variants in exon 6 of CSNK1A1.

entries.proposition: Patient 1 had multiple congenital anomalies and died at one year; the phenotype is not isolated spasms.
entries.snippet: The child died of severe malnutrition at 1 year of age.

entries.proposition: Patient 1 congenital anomalies listed (heart, eye, chest wall).
entries.snippet: Cardiac ultrasound suggested congenital heart disease, manifested by cardiac ventricular septal defect, unclosed ductus arteriosus, and unclosed oval hole.

entries.proposition: Patient 2: seizures controlled with attacks every 3-6 months; intellectual and attention problems at eight years.
entries.snippet: The epileptic seizures were controlled but occurred once every 3–6 months.

entries.proposition: Treatment sentence names "vinyl chloride" as an antiseizure agent, which is evidently a translation error for an unnamed drug; the treatment history cannot be read as stated.
entries.snippet: the spasms were slightly controlled by treatment with adrenocorticotropic hormone, sodium valproate, topiramate, and vinyl chloride.

entries.proposition: Only the missense variant lowered CSNK1A1 mRNA and protein in the overexpression assay; the deletion did not.
entries.snippet: The results of qPCR and Western blot assays demonstrated that Mut remarkably reduced CSNK1A1 gene expression on both mRNA and protein level. However, no significant difference was observed between WT and Del despite the slight decreasing trend (Fig. 2F–H).

entries.proposition: Co-IP reduction of beta-catenin binding and raised beta-catenin level are the central mechanistic claim.
entries.snippet: The results of immunoprecipitation indicated that, in both Mut and Del, the interaction between CSNK1A1 and β-catenin was considerably decreased (Fig. 3E).

entries.proposition: Beta-catenin was raised in cells expressing either variant, with the missense higher than the deletion; the comparator is wild-type CSNK1A1 overexpression.
entries.snippet: Moreover, the intracellular level of β-catenin was strongly enhanced in both variants (Fig. 3F and G)

entries.proposition: MYC and CCND1 transcripts were higher with either variant; AXIN2 only with the missense.
entries.snippet: Therefore, we performed qPCR on genes AXIN2, MYC and CCND1 and observed significantly higher expression levels of MYC and CCND1 in both Mut and Del.

entries.proposition: Proliferation was measured as EdU incorporation in HEK-293T cells.
entries.snippet: Compared with the WT, the EdU positive rates (percentage of cells that had undergone cell division) in cells transfected with Mut and Del were elevated (Fig. 4A and B).

entries.proposition: The authors declare the model limits: small sample and in vitro only, mechanism incomplete.
entries.snippet: In vitro experiments, while providing valuable insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms, cannot fully recapitulate the complex physiological environment of the human body.

entries.proposition: Method: HEK-293T transfected with GFP-tagged CSNK1A1 cDNA; the cells carry endogenous wild-type CSNK1A1, and there is no empty-vector arm in the text.
entries.snippet: HEK-293 T cells were transfected with EGFP-tagged CSNK1A1 and Flag-CTNNB1plasmids.

entries.proposition: Statement that the mutations are expected to be loss of function is a prediction before the assays.
entries.snippet: The mutation sites of both variants are within the kinase domain of CSNK1A1, and they were therefore expected to show loss-of-function effects, which are speculated to be pathogenic.

entries.proposition: Supplement Table 1 lists fourteen other variants in the patients (the table does not say which patient), including a de novo frameshift in ACTN1 and a TSC1 variant classed likely pathogenic, described as not directly linked to the phenotype.
entries.snippet: Table 1. Genetic variants not directly linked to the clinical phenotype of the ISS patients

entries.proposition: The supplement note admits that listed variants may relate to the phenotype and cannot be excluded.
entries.snippet: The listed variants may be related to the patient's clinical phenotype, but cannot fully explain the clinical presentation.

entries.proposition: Fig 4B-C: EdU-positive rate WT about 20 percent, Mut about 36 (***), Del about 30 (*); qPCR bars about 1.25-1.5 fold with a single star; CTNNB1 mRNA unchanged; image fields differ in cell density between conditions.

entries.proposition: Fig 1A-B: pedigrees show Family 1 with a single affected child and Family 2 with an affected son and unaffected brother (matching the text). The Family_1 proband trace in 1B shows overlapping peaks over a multi-base stretch (the pattern of a heterozygous multi-base indel) and the Family_2 proband trace a single-base change, whereas the text assigns the missense to patient 1 and the deletion to patient 2; panel labels do not name the variants. Adjudication of the assignment is owed to a blind audit.
